about.title: San Gabriel Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash on Valley Boulevard, Del Mar Avenue, or another San Gabriel corridor takes a loved one's life, the grief is immediate but the legal questions often aren't. Public crash records show San Gabriel logs traffic deaths and hundreds of injury collisions each year, with reported crashes clustering on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. Behind each of those numbers is a family trying to figure out what comes next. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects grieving families in San Gabriel with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain your options under California law, and help you understand whether a claim may be appropriate for your situation, all without any fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What San Gabriel Families Should Know

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, prioritizing a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some cases. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Quickly
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Waiting to speak with someone can cost your family options.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help you understand what applies to your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in San Gabriel?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of death to file, though claims involving a government entity or public roadway often require a much earlier claim notice. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to speak with an attorney as soon as you're able. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can walk through the timeline that applies to your family's case.

items.question: Which corridors in San Gabriel see the most reported crashes?
items.answer: Public collision records point to San Gabriel Boulevard, Del Mar Avenue, Las Tunas Drive, and Valley Boulevard as higher-volume corridors, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. These are simply record-based patterns, not a judgment about any specific location. If a loved one was lost on one of these roads, an independent attorney can look into the details of what happened.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action seeking compensation for the surviving family, even if criminal charges are filed against the at-fault party, and even if they aren't. The two proceedings run independently and have different standards of proof. An attorney can explain how any related criminal matter might intersect with your civil claim.
